newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on Lujiazui swings.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on Lujiazui swings.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down on Monday, with market barometre Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development recovering dramatically just before the close, brokers said.

The index ended down 0.089 or 0.17 percent to 51.093 points, after hitting an intra-day low of 50.368, on volume of 9.8 million shares worth $4.3 million. Of 41 B shares, 33 traded, with 14 down, nine flat and 10 up.
Brokers said that late buying by institutions pushed up Shanghai Lujiazui, so it recovered morning losses, enabling the index to make up most of its losses.
But market sentiment remained weak on a lack of follow-up buying, they added.
Shanghai Lujiazui traded the most and ended up $0.002 or 0.21 percent to $0.930, after hitting an intra-day low of $0.880, on volume of 2.1 million shares.
"Buying of Lujiazui mainly came from domestic institutions but overseas selling was still heavy," one broker said.
"Most investors have lost confidence in building positions because of market uncertainties," he added.
"The index will fall further in the next few days despite institutional support," a second broker said.
Shanghai Goods & Materials was the biggest loser, down $0.010 or 7.57 percent to $0.122, on volume of 67,000 shares.
Heilongjiang Electric Power followed on profit-taking, dropping $0.016 or 4.21 percent to $0.364, on volume of 721,400 shares.
Shanghai A share ended down on a correction in active trade, with players hunting for shares of recently listed companies, brokers said.
The index lost 8.184 points or 0.98 percent to 829.778 points, on volume of 330.7 million shares worth 3.3 billion yuan. The SSE 30 fell 19.709 points or 0.91 percent to 2145.585 points.
Huayin Electric was the biggest loser on profit-taking, tumbling 1.38 yuan or 7.59 percent to 16.80 yuan, on volume of 11.5 million shares.
